title: Stomach trouble and finding cooks who could feed him
summary: Thomas explains he left Hopkins partly because of hyperacidity and tension in 1936. He relied on friendly cooks in the Dakotas who prepared light food for him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, listen, why do you leave Hop now? What happened to him? According to this guy ...
My stomach's getting pretty good. I think my stomach I met Babe, got better and I had a lot of trouble in '36. Well,
you have to put that down because ...
... Time with me because I might have raped her when she was a little girl, ho, ho, ho.
Well, what happened that summer was very bad and I had a lot of trouble.
What did you have? Ulcers or what?

No, it was really designed (sic), what they tell me now, as hyperacidity and tension and all that kind of thing. Anyhow, it was troublesome so I had to go through ... But, with the trumpet what happened with me I could pick up the instrument, which I always do, and feel as if my chops were just full. And I couldn't digest my food. And, my food had gotten out of (clicks his fingers) out of ideas. I had people up in Minnesota through the Dakotas. I was very fortunate. I knew some chefs up there, too. And that's before I joined Fats' band. Maybe it gave me some ideas. Some fellows up there in a place like Montevideo and Otoclidic (?), Ottawa and they prepared things for on me.
